sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain by Siegfried Arno. “Ach, Otto, Otto…!” Foxtrot. Electrola EG 2135 A, matrix BD 9264-2; issued January 1931. Discographic entry in Henry König’s Electrola label list, citing Discographie der deutschen Kleinkunst, vol. 1, p. 27.
sources.title: Ach, Otto, Otto…! — Electrola EG 2135
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester; Siegfried Arno, refrain vocal
sources.researchNote: The primary link leads directly to Henry König’s Electrola label list. Its EG 2135 A entry names Marek Weber and Siegfried Arno, matrix BD 9264-2, duration 3:12, the Beethoven-Saal in Berlin, release in January 1931 and the alternative issue HMV AM 3450. It cites Discographie der deutschen Kleinkunst, vol. 1, p. 27. The session field supplies a venue but no recording date; January 1931 is therefore an issue month, not a session date. The corresponding listening reference does not independently establish the pressing or take reproduced.

sources.shortCitation: Electrola EG 2228, “Ich steh’ im Schnee und wart’ auf Dich” (Mitja Nikisch with Paul Dorn, 1931)
sources.fullCitation: Mitja Nikisch und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Paul Dorn. “Ich steh’ im Schnee und wart’ auf Dich.” Foxtrot from Die grosse Attraktion. Electrola E.G. 2228, matrix OD106-2, recorded Berlin, 15 March 1931; also issued as His Master’s Voice AM 3411 and HMV R 14602. Electrola label and title lists at musiktiteldb.de, following the Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik, vol. 4.
sources.title: Ich steh’ im Schnee und wart’ auf Dich — Electrola EG 2228
sources.creator: Mitja Nikisch und sein Orchester; Paul Dorn, refrain vocal
sources.researchNote: The discographic entry assigns both words and music to Bronisław Kaper. Hofmeister (February 1931, p. 35) registers the song under Kaper with words by Fritz Rotter and Armin Robinson; the discographic lyric credit is not used to replace that. The Electrola label list gives 15 March 1931 in its recording-date column and leaves the release-date column empty. HMV R 14602 is a parallel record issue, not a U.S. copyright renewal identifier.

sources.fullCitation: Guy Lombardo. “Ninon.” Decca 466, matrix DLA-144, recorded Los Angeles, 23 March 1935. Title list at musiktiteldb.de, compiled by Henry König from discographic and trade sources.
sources.title: Ninon — Decca 466
sources.creator: Guy Lombardo
sources.researchNote: The title-list entry gives Los Angeles, 23 March 1935, as the recording place and date and leaves the release-date column empty; the structured date therefore describes the session, not the issue of Decca 466. The entry credits Kaper and Jurmann for the music and Harold Adamson for the words. That combination supports identifying this record as the English-language version of the song written for Ein Lied für dich.

sources.shortCitation: Gloria G.O. 10155, “Mondnacht in Sanssouci” (Eric Harden with John Hendrik, 1931)
sources.fullCitation: Eric Harden und sein Tanz-Orchester, refrain sung by John Hendrik. “Mondnacht in Sanssouci.” Gloria G.O. 10155, matrix Bi 80, recorded 29 April 1931. Title list at musiktiteldb.de, compiled by Henry König from discographic and trade sources.
sources.title: Mondnacht in Sanssouci — Gloria G.O. 10155
sources.creator: Eric Harden und sein Tanz-Orchester; John Hendrik, refrain vocal
sources.researchNote: The title-list entry gives 29 April 1931 as the recording date and leaves the release-date column empty. The structured date therefore identifies the session, not the commercial issue of Gloria G.O. 10155. No publicly accessible transfer of this disc was located during the recording-link audit.

sources.shortCitation: Grammophon 885 B, “Eine Sommernacht am Meer” (Fred Marley Orchestra, 1932)
sources.fullCitation: Fred Marley und sein Tanz-Orchester, with Leo Monosson identified as refrain vocalist. “Eine Sommernacht am Meer.” Grammophon 885 B, matrix 1703 BN3; recorded at the Schumannsaal, Berlin, 15 August 1932. Music credited to Bob Handers; words by Fritz Rotter. Labelliste “Grammophon” (1931–1932), based on Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik, vol. 8, at musiktiteldb.de.
sources.title: Eine Sommernacht am Meer — Grammophon 885 B
sources.creator: Fred Marley und sein Tanz-Orchester; Leo Monosson, refrain vocal
sources.researchNote: Bob Handers was the joint recording pseudonym used by Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann.

sources.shortCitation: Gloria G.O. 10303, “Wie gern möcht’ ich dich verwöhnen” (1932)
sources.fullCitation: Eric Harden und sein Tanz-Orchester, refrain sung by Carljohann Volbach. “Wie gern möcht’ ich dich verwöhnen!” From Melodie der Liebe; music by Walter Jurmann and Bronislaw Kaper, words by Fritz Rotter. Gloria G.O. 10303, matrix Bi 644. Recorded in Berlin, studio 4, 11 June 1932; issued November 1932. Title-list entry at Musiktiteldb.de, citing Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik, vol. 8.
sources.title: Wie gern möcht’ ich dich verwöhnen — Gloria G.O. 10303
sources.creator: Eric Harden und sein Tanz-Orchester; Carljohann Volbach, refrain vocal
sources.researchNote: The title-list entry distinguishes the recording session (Berlin, studio 4, 11 June 1932) from the Gloria issue (November 1932). This source documents Gloria G.O. 10303 specifically. The Internet Archive transfer numbered D 4431 reports the same matrix, Bi 644, but does not identify its issuing label or date; the Gloria imprint and November issue date are not assigned to that pressing. No second listening reference is created.
